annotation.title_clean: Opinion 28/2024 on certain data protection aspects related to the processing of personal data in the context of AI models
annotation.title_en: Opinion 28/2024 on certain data protection aspects related to the processing of personal data in the context of AI models
annotation.summary_en: EDPB opinion, requested by the Irish supervisory authority under Article 64(2) GDPR, on personal data in AI models. It covers when a model can be considered anonymous, how legitimate interest can be relied on in development and deployment, and what unlawful training means for later use. It is general AI with no embodied content.
key_provisions_or_claims: AI models trained on personal data cannot in all cases be considered anonymous; supervisory authorities assess this case by case.
Anonymity requires that the likelihood of extracting personal data or obtaining it from queries is insignificant, using all means reasonably likely to be used.
Legitimate interest relies on a three-step test (legitimate interest, necessity, balancing), and mitigating measures can tip the balance.
Controllers must document and test for anonymity (membership inference, regurgitation, model inversion) to meet accountability under Article 5(2).
Unlawful development processing can affect lawfulness of deployment depending on the scenario; a truly anonymised model falls outside the GDPR.
